title: Visitor in the Dark Night
next_chapter_hook: Mo Xiansheng's remnant soul dissipated slowly, but his words exploded in Chen Ji's mind like thunder—the fate of Chapter 700 was not an ending, but a beginning. What did that truly mean?

text.content:
The aftershocks of Heavenly Punishment had not yet faded, yet Chen Ji discovered new patterns emerging on the Tianji Record Fragment—the patterns were not a blessing, but a mark etched into his very bones, meaning his entanglement with the Heavenly Eye had only just begun.

At midnight, in the servants' quarters of the Tianqing Sect Back Mountain, Chen Ji sat alone on a dilapidated wooden bed. His fingertips brushed across the yellowed pages of the Tianji Record, and the newly emerged patterns faintly radiated a chill, as if something was gazing through those thin pages, watching his every move.

He took a deep breath, forcing himself to remain calm. His Heavenly Fate was down to 43 points—every use of foresight brought him closer to death, yet these new patterns seemed like an ominous premonition, reminding him that the Heavenly Eye had never abandoned its control over him.

Outside the window, the night wind rose abruptly, causing the worn paper screens to rustle. Just as Chen Ji was about to close the book, a wisp of blue smoke rose gently from the first page of the Tianji Record, coalescing beneath the moonlight into a hazy silhouette.

dialogue.content:
"Greetings, Young Master. Long time no see."

The voice was ancient and ethereal, as if traveling from an impossibly distant void, carrying an ineffable sense of vicissitude. The smoky figure gradually solidified—a white-haired elder with a gaunt yet profound face, whose eyes held a terrifying depth.

Chen Ji's pupils constricted sharply. His hand instinctively tightened around the Tianji Record, his body tensing instantly—an ingrained reflex developed over years of survival, ensuring his safety before facing any unknown threat.

"Who are you?" Chen Ji's voice was unnervingly calm. "A remnant soul from the first page of the Tianji Record? Or yet another existence seeking to exploit me?"

Mo Xiansheng's form wavered slightly, as if苦笑ing. "The Young Master is indeed cautious. Excellent. In this world, caution is the foremost requirement for survival."

text.content:
Moonlight filtered through the torn window screens, casting mottled shadows on the ground. Mo Xiansheng's remnant soul floated motionless in mid-air, surrounded by a faint azure Spiritual Light—weak yet pure, entirely unlike the sinister aura Chen Ji associated with the Demonic Path.

Chen Ji narrowed his eyes, studying this uninvited guest. His spiritual sense reached out silently, attempting to gauge the other's cultivation depth—yet the remnant soul was like an unfathomable abyss. His spiritual sense entered it like a clay ox vanishing into the sea, stirring not even a ripple.

This sensation, Chen Ji had only experienced with one person—Tianqing Sect's former Master, Ling Yuan. But the depth of this remnant soul seemed to surpass even Ling Yuan's.

"Three years." Mo Xiansheng suddenly spoke, his voice carrying a barely perceptible sigh. "This old servant has waited three years for the moment the Young Master would unseal the third page."

dialogue.content:
"Three years?" Chen Ji's voice cooled. "You've been by my side for three years, and I noticed nothing."

His fingers subtly formed seals within his sleeve, a subtle formation pattern taking shape at his feet. This was one of the self-preservation techniques he'd learned from the Tianji Record—the "Deceiving Heaven Art," capable of temporarily masking one's aura and confusing enemies' perception.

Yet Mo Xiansheng merely glanced at him indifferently, his gaze seemingly capable of piercing through all pretense. "The Young Master need not be nervous. If this old servant harbored harmful intentions, you would never have survived until today. For three years, this old servant watched the Young Master systematically place pieces across the three great sects, secretly positioning chess pieces everywhere. Such temperament and strategy have not disappointed this old servant's former master's expectations."

A faint glint flickered in Chen Ji's eyes. "Your 'former master'—who is that?"

Mo Xiansheng fell silent for a moment, as if weighing how to respond. Beneath the moonlight, his form grew increasingly ethereal, as if he might dissipate into the void at any moment.

"My master... was named Chen Xuan." Mo Xiansheng's voice was low and solemn. "He was the previous holder of the Tianji Record, and the Young Master's father."

The words struck like thunder in Chen Ji's mind. His breath caught for an instant before quickly stabilizing—years of feigning had taught him to remain composed under any circumstances.

"I never met my father." Chen Ji's voice was terrifyingly composed. "He disappeared before I was born. My mother never mentioned him."

Mo Xiansheng sighed. "That is because someone wished to prevent the Young Master from learning the truth. To protect you, Master entrusted you to your mother and then embarked alone on the path of opposing the Heavenly Eye. He knew that upon his death, the Heavenly Eye would certainly root out any trace. Thus, he sealed his inheritance, memories, and power within the Tianji Record, awaiting the Young Master's awakening."

text.content:
The night wind passed through the worn window frames, carrying a bone-piercing chill. Chen Ji stood in place, listening to Mo Xiansheng's account with an impassive expression, while his heart churned like stormy waves.

Chen Xuan. The previous holder of the Tianji Record. His father.

This information fragmented and rapidly reassembled in his mind, yet still could not form a complete picture. All he knew was that from his earliest memories, his mother had raised him alone, never mentioning anything about his father. He had always attributed his eligibility for the Tianji Record to some coincidence or bloodline inheritance.

But now, Mo Xiansheng claimed it was all arranged?

"You claim to be my father's... guardian?" Chen Ji's voice turned slightly hoarse. "Then why reveal yourself only now? Have you been protecting me in secret these three years? Protecting what?"

dialogue.content:
Mo Xiansheng's form wavered slightly, as if struggling against some invisible force.

"This old servant is merely a remnant soul with limited power." His voice grew increasingly ethereal. "Three years ago, when the Young Master first awakened the Tianji Record, your power was far too weak to withstand too much truth. Had this old servant appeared then, it would only have drawn the Heavenly Eye's premature attention, bringing catastrophic disaster."

"So you watched me get bullied in the sect?" Coldness crept into Chen Ji's voice. "The servant identity, the humiliation, the mockery—you knew about all of it?"

Mo Xiansheng fell silent for a long moment before speaking slowly. "Every hardship the Young Master endured, this old servant witnessed. But this old servant also knew those difficulties were precisely the foundation of the Young Master's growth. Without those years of hardship, the Young Master would never have developed such cautious, resilient character, nor survived in this cutthroat cultivation world until today."

Chen Ji冷笑一声. "倒是你的'苦心'了."

text.content:
Mo Xiansheng showed no anger at Chen Ji's sarcasm, merely floating quietly in mid-air, azure Spiritual Light circulating slowly around him.

"The Young Master's resentment, this old servant understands." His voice was peaceful yet sincere. "But some things must be personally experienced before one can truly comprehend their meaning. The cultivation world has never been a peaceful realm. Had the Young Master stood in the spotlight from the start, you would have become a pawn in the struggles of various powers long ago, rather than the meticulous chess master you are today."

Chen Ji remained silent, but his expression softened slightly. He had to admit Mo Xiansheng had a point. Without years of patience and accumulation, he could never have reached where he was in this dog-eat-dog world.

However, understanding was one thing; trust was another.

"You revealed yourself tonight surely not merely to tell me these things." Chen Ji's voice returned to calm. "Speak. What do you want?"

dialogue.content:
Mo Xiansheng's form suddenly drifted forward, closing much of the distance between them. Beneath the moonlight, those profound eyes in his face gleamed with an ineffable light.

"The Young Master is indeed wise." Mo Xiansheng's voice turned solemn. "This old servant appears tonight because of the new patterns on the Tianji Record—they are the Heavenly Eye's mark. From this moment, it has locked onto the Young Master's location. No matter where the Young Master goes, it can perceive your aura."

Chen Ji's heart sank heavily. He looked down at the patterns on the Tianji Record and indeed saw those newly emerged lines pulsing faintly, as if some lifeform writhed within them.

"Is there a way to break it?" he asked deeply.

Mo Xiansheng smiled faintly, yet that smile carried a hint of bitterness. "There are two methods. First, fully awakening the Tianji Record—the complete Tianji Record can shield the Heavenly Eye's perception; second—"

text.content:
"What is the second?" Chen Ji pressed.

Mo Xiansheng deliberated for a moment,似乎在权衡着什么. Finally, he spoke slowly. "The second method is—this old servant can help the Young Master transfer this mark. This old servant's remnant soul can temporarily bear this karma, causing the Heavenly Eye's perception to deviate, buying the Young Master some time."

"The cost?" Chen Ji stared directly into Mo Xiansheng's eyes. "There are no free meals in this world. You must pay a price for helping me transfer this mark."

Mo Xiansheng's form shuddered slightly. He seemed unprepared for Chen Ji to see through this so directly, but quickly a gratified smile appeared on his face.

"The Young Master has truly matured." Mo Xiansheng sighed. "Yes, the cost is this old servant's remaining remnant soul power. If choosing this path, this old servant will completely dissipate in one month, never again able to provide any assistance to the Young Master."

choice.prompt: Facing the two choices Mo Xiansheng presented, Chen Ji needed to decide: to fully trust this remnant soul claiming to be his father's guardian, or to remain vigilant and first probe for more information?

choices.description: Although doubts lingered, Mo Xiansheng's words were the only solution available. Chen Ji decided to temporarily accept his help while secretly observing.
choices.risk_hint: Mo Xiansheng may have ulterior motives

dialogue.content: Chen Ji fell silent for a moment, then slowly nodded. "Very well, I trust you. But I have one condition—within this one month, you will tell me everything you know. About the Tianji Record, about my father, about the Heavenly Eye, about everything I must know."

text.content:
Mo Xiansheng's form shuddered slightly, as if unprepared for Chen Ji to decide so干脆利落. After a moment, a gratified smile appeared on his face, carrying a sense of relieved ease.

"Thank you for trusting the Young Master." Mo Xiansheng bowed deeply. "Rest assured, this old servant will share everything without reservation, holding nothing back."

choices.description: Chen Ji would not easily trust anyone, especially this suddenly appearing mysterious existence. He decided to use questions to probe Mo Xiansheng's true identity and purpose.
choices.risk_hint: Mo Xiansheng may leave due to lack of trust

dialogue.content: Chen Ji did not answer immediately. Instead, he slowly closed the Tianji Record, his gaze sharp as a blade as he stared at Mo Xiansheng: "You claim to be my father's guardian, but how can I be certain you're telling the truth? For three years you've been hiding within the Tianji Record—who's to say you're not another existence trying to exploit me?"

Mo Xiansheng remained unperturbed, merely offering a subtle smile. "The young master is indeed prudent. That's commendable. This old servant was about to provide some evidence."

With that, he casually gestured, and a wisp of azure Spiritual Light spiraled from his fingertip, merging into Chen Ji's brow. Within that ethereal radiance were fragmented visions—a white-robed man cradling an infant, his eyes brimming with tenderness; the same man standing atop a mountain summit, confronting swirling dark clouds with unwavering resolve; and a letter bearing sparse words: "My son Chen Ji, if you can read this letter, it means your father has already departed this world..."

Chen Ji stood frozen.

Those visions were too authentic, so real that his heart couldn't help but pound violently. In the scenes, the white-robed man appeared handsome, his bearing gentle and refined, his lips always carrying a faint smile—that smile bore an uncanny resemblance to what Chen Ji saw in his own reflection in the bronze mirror.

"These are memories the master left for the young master," Mo Xiansheng's voice softened considerably. "The master never abandoned you, young master. His departure was a necessity. Only by leaving could he divert the attention of the Heavenly Eye, buying you time to grow."

Chen Ji drew a deep breath, forcing himself to remain calm. Yet his voice still trembled slightly: "Then where is he now?"

Mo Xiansheng fell silent.

That silence spoke louder than any words. Chen Ji felt as though something had violently struck a place deep within his heart, the pain nearly suffocating him.

"The master..." Mo Xiansheng finally spoke, his voice carrying boundless sorrow, "perished together with the Heavenly Eye."

The night wind surged, rustling the withered branches outside the window. Chen Ji stood motionless, as if stripped of all strength. His mind kept echoing Mo Xiansheng's words—mutual destruction.

So his father had chosen that path of no return to protect him.

So none of the "coincidences" he'd experienced over the years were coincidences at all—they were the path his father had paved with his life.

Chen Ji closed his eyes, breathing deeply. When he opened them again, those eyes had regained their usual tranquility, though within their depths burned an unprecedented fire.

text.content:
"The Heavenly Eye is not dead." Chen Ji's voice was low and ice-cold. "It merely suffered mutual injury with my father and is now recuperating. Once it recovers, it will return—and I am its next target."

Mo Xiansheng nodded approvingly: "The young master is indeed intelligent. The master's confrontation with the Heavenly Eye all those years ago never truly reached a conclusion. In that battle, the Heavenly Eye's power was greatly diminished, forcing it into slumber; while the master's soul was shattered beyond reformation. But the master knew the Heavenly Eye would not relent, so he placed all his hopes upon the young master."

Chen Ji lowered his gaze to the Tianji Record in his hands, its patterns seeming to sense his emotions, emitting a faint glow.

"So the marking on this Tianji Record is the Heavenly Eye declaring sovereignty?" he asked.

Mo Xiansheng nodded: "One could say so. The Heavenly Eye has already detected the young master's existence—this mark is its marker. From now on, it will constantly observe every move the young master makes, until it finds the opportunity to utterly erase the young master."

Chen Ji's fingers gently traced those patterns, deep in thought.

"How did my father confront the Heavenly Eye back then?" he suddenly asked. "What kind of power does the complete form of the Tianji Record possess?"

Mo Xiansheng's form wavered slightly, as if hesitating to speak. After a moment, he still answered: "The complete form of the Tianji Record is called the 'Tianji Complete Text.' It contains information about the past, present, and future three realms, allowing its holder to glimpse the trajectory of fate. However—"

He paused, his voice growing especially grave: "But the Tianji Complete Text has a fatal flaw. Each use consumes a tremendous amount of Heavenly Fate. When Heavenly Fate is exhausted, so too is the holder's soul—obliterated."

Chen Ji's gaze hardened slightly: "So that's why my father..."

"The master used the Tianji Complete Text countless times throughout his life, solely to find a path to defeat the Heavenly Eye." Mo Xiansheng sighed. "But in the end, he never found that path."

choice.prompt: Mo Xiansheng presented two choices: one was to fully awaken the Tianji Record, though it would require an enormous price; the other was to have Mo Xiansheng transfer the mark, though he would dissipate as a result. Would one month be sufficient for Chen Ji to make a decision?

choices.description: Choose to fully awaken the Tianji Record. The complete Tianji Record can shield against the Heavenly Eye's perception. This requires Chen Ji to complete a certain major task within one month.
choices.visible_cost: Must complete an almost impossible task within one month
choices.visible_reward: Obtain the complete Tianji Record and completely escape the Heavenly Eye's tracking
choices.risk_hint: Failure will lead to utter destruction

dialogue.content:
"I choose to awaken the Tianji Record." Chen Ji's voice was resolute. "The path my father spent a lifetime unable to find doesn't mean I cannot find it either. Besides—"

A cold smile curved his lips: "I never believed there is any absolute deadlock in this world. What people call a deadlock is simply not yet having found the key to breaking the situation."

text.content:
Mo Xiansheng gazed at Chen Ji, a complex light flickering in his eyes—gratification, worry, and a hint of barely perceptible anticipation.

"The young master truly possesses the master's spirit from years ago." He spoke slowly. "Since the young master has made the decision, this old servant shall reveal the method to awaken the Tianji Record—the young master must collect three ancient artifacts within one month: the 'Abyssal Mirror,' the treasured artifact of the Xuanwu Sect; the forbidden technique scroll from the Holy Sect of the Demonic Path; and—the 'Seed of Destiny' hidden deep within the Forbidden Grounds of the Tianqing Sect."

choices.text: Have Mo Xiansheng transfer the mark
choices.description: Accept Mo Xiansheng's sacrifice and let him transfer the Heavenly Eye's mark. This buys one month of buffer time, but the cost is losing Mo Xiansheng.
choices.visible_cost: Lose Mo Xiansheng, this important guardian
choices.visible_reward: Gain one month of safe time to plan at leisure
choices.risk_hint: Will face the Heavenly Eye alone after one month

dialogue.content:
Chen Ji fell silent for a long while. When he spoke again, there was a barely perceptible tremor in his voice: "No, I cannot let you die for me. You claim to be my father's guardian, then you should live even more—live to help me accomplish my father's unfinished endeavor."

Mo Xiansheng froze, seemingly not expecting Chen Ji to say such words. After a moment, his eyes actually glistened with a faint sheen of tears.

text.content:
"Young master..." Mo Xiansheng's voice choked. "If the master looks down from the underworld, he will surely be proud of the young master."

Chen Ji shook his head: "I need no one's pride. I only know that in this world, having one more person who can help me is worth far more than having one more shade that needs my protection."

dialogue.content:
Mo Xiansheng wiped the corner of his eye, his expression becoming serious once more.

"Since the young master's resolve is set, this old servant shall reveal another method." He deliberated. "Actually, there is a middle-ground solution—the young master could first awaken a portion of the Tianji Record, while having this old servant help transfer part of the mark. This way, the young master will have some self-protection capability, and this old servant can accompany the young master for a while longer."

Chen Ji raised an eyebrow: "What risks does this approach carry?"

Mo Xiansheng苦笑: "The risk is that the transferred mark can only hold for three months. After three months, the mark will return to the young master, and by then the Heavenly Eye's perception will be even sharper than now."

Chen Ji nodded thoughtfully. This solution, while not perfect, could at least buy him more time to strategize.

"What if I choose the first option?" he asked. "Collecting the three artifacts within one month—what's the actual probability of success?"

text.content:
Mo Xiansheng deliberated for a moment, then spoke slowly: "Based on the young master's current abilities and resources, the success rate is less than ten percent."

Chen Ji remained silent, gazing steadily at Mo Xiansheng.

"However—" Mo Xiansheng turned the tables, "if the young master can leverage the strength of various factions, this success rate can be raised to thirty percent. And if the young master can break through another realm within this month, the success rate will exceed fifty percent."

Chen Ji lowered his head in contemplation, his fingers gently tapping the Tianji Record's cover. His mind raced through possibilities—the Abyssal Mirror from the Xuanwu Sect was Han Lie's territory; the forbidden technique scroll from the Holy Sect of the Demonic Path might find assistance through Ye Qing; and the Seed of Destiny within the Tianqing Sect was located at the deepest part, the domain of the former Sect Leader Ling Yuan.

Three artifacts, three of the hardest bones to chew.

Chen Ji suddenly smiled, that grin carrying a hint of dangerous intrigue: "Interesting."

dialogue.content:
"What has the young master thought of?" Mo Xiansheng asked.

Chen Ji did not answer directly, but asked instead: "Among the three artifacts, which one do you think is most difficult to obtain?"

Mo Xiansheng considered: "The Abyssal Mirror. It is the Xuanwu Sect's treasured artifact, protected by层层禁制—countless layers of formations and restrictions. Unless the Sect Master himself agrees, it is fundamentally impossible to obtain."

"Then what do you think would make the Xuanwu Sect Master agree?"

Mo Xiansheng froze, then suddenly realized: "The young master intends to...form an alliance with the Xuanwu Sect?"

Chen Ji nodded: "That fool Han Lie is an eyesore, but the Xuanwu Sect Master is a shrewd individual. If we can offer sufficient筹码—sufficient bargaining chips—we may not be unable to secure temporary use of the Abyssal Mirror."

choice.prompt: Chen Ji must make a choice among the three artifacts—which one to pursue first? Different choices will determine the direction of subsequent actions and the allies that can be recruited.

choices.description: Choose to start with the Xuanming Mirror from Xuanwu Sect. This requires dealing with Han Lie and Xuanwu Sect, the process may be tortuous, but the rewards after success are the greatest.
choices.visible_cost: Must face Han Lie's provocation and Xuanwu Sect's pressure
choices.visible_reward: Gain Xuanwu Sect's support, greatly enhance strength and reputation
choices.risk_hint: May have direct confrontation with Han Lie

text.content:
Chen Ji rose from his seat, walked to the window, gazing at the whitening horizon in the distant sky. His gaze was deep and cold, as if looking at a massive chessboard.

"Han Lie..." he murmured to himself, "that self-righteous fool, probably never dreamed that one day he would voluntarily bring the Xuanming Mirror to my hands."

Mo Xiansheng was slightly stunned: "What does the young master intend to do?"

Chen Ji turned around, a meaningful smile curving his lips: "Simple. I will make Han Lie realize that without me, he is nothing. When he's driven to a dead end, the Xuanming Mirror will naturally fall into my hands."

choices.text: First, obtain the Forbidden Technique Fragment
choices.description: Choose to start with the Holy Sect of the Demonic Path. This requires cooperating with Ye Qing, the risk is the greatest, but Ye Qing's abilities are crucial for concealing the aura of the Tianji Record.
choices.visible_cost: May expose the relationship with the Demonic Path
choices.visible_reward: Gain Ye Qing's full support, master the method to conceal the Tianji Record's aura
choices.risk_hint: The Holy Maiden of the Demonic Path may have other intentions

dialogue.content:
Chen Ji turned to Mo Xiansheng: "Regarding Ye Qing, I have my own arrangements. Although the Holy Sect of the Demonic Path is dangerous, Ye Qing has a reason she must cooperate with me - the day the Holy Sect treats her as a discarded pawn is the day she will come to me."

Mo Xiansheng nodded: "The young master speaks wisely. Although the Holy Sect of the Demonic Path's Forbidden Technique Fragment is dangerous, the 'Demon Path Fog' in Ye Qing's hands can indeed effectively conceal the Tianji Record's aura. This point is crucial for the young master."

choices.text: First, obtain the Seed of Destiny
choices.description: Choose to start with the Tianqing Sect's Forbidden Grounds. This is the environment Chen Ji is most familiar with, but the old Sect Master Ling Yuan is watching from the shadows, the risk is equally immense.
choices.visible_cost: May disturb the snake, exposing ambitions
choices.visible_reward: Acting on one's own territory is more convenient, and can further control the Tianqing Sect
choices.risk_hint: The old Sect Master Ling Yuan has been watching with predatory intent

dialogue.content:
Chen Ji contemplated briefly: "The Tianqing Sect's Forbidden Grounds... the Seed of Destiny. That is the old Sect Master Ling Yuan's territory, sneaking in undetected will not be easy."

Mo Xiansheng smiled faintly: "The young master should not forget, although this old servant is merely a remnant soul, I am thoroughly familiar with the Tianqing Sect's formations. Back then, the master once brought this old servant deep into the Forbidden Grounds, where there exists an unknown secret passage."

Chen Ji's eyes lit up slightly: "You mean—"

"Exactly. That secret passage was opened by the master himself back then. Besides this old servant, no second person knows of it."

text.content:
The eastern horizon had begun to glow with a silvery white, the dawn's first light about to pierce through the night. Mo Xiansheng's form had become increasingly faint, blue spiritual light flickering gently around him.

"Young master, time is running out." Mo Xiansheng's voice grew somewhat ethereal, "This old servant's remnant soul power cannot be sustained much longer. Before it dissipates completely, this old servant has one final secret to tell the young master."

Chen Ji raised his head, his gaze blazing: "What secret?"

Mo Xiansheng gazed deeply at Chen Ji, speaking word by word: "The Eye of Heavenly Mandate is not invincible. Its weakness lies hidden within the fate of Chapter Seven Hundred."

Chen Ji's pupils contracted sharply: "Chapter Seven Hundred? The words you said before—fate of Chapter Seven Hundred is not an ending, but a beginning—that's what you meant?"

dialogue.content:
Mo Xiansheng's form had become so faint it was nearly transparent, but he still struggled to maintain his shape, his eyes filled with complex emotions.

"Young master, the master spent his entire life searching for a method to defeat the Eye of Heavenly Mandate. He discovered that the Eye of Heavenly Mandate's power comes from living beings' fear of destiny—as long as living beings still fear destiny, the Eye of Heavenly Mandate will grow stronger."

Chen Ji furrowed his brow: "Then isn't that unsolvable? As long as humans exist, there will inevitably be fear of destiny."

Mo Xiansheng shook his head: "No, the young master has thought incorrectly. The master discovered that the Eye of Heavenly Mandate has a fatal weakness—it can only perceive those beings recorded within destiny. In other words, if someone can break free from outside of destiny, the Eye of Heavenly Mandate cannot perceive them."

Chen Ji's breathing quickened slightly: "Break free from outside of destiny? How is that possible?"

Mo Xiansheng smiled faintly, that smile carrying a hint of anticipation: "The master did not find the method, but this old servant believes the young master will surely find it. Because the young master's destiny, from the very beginning, was never recorded."

Mo Xiansheng's form finally dissipated completely, leaving only a wisp of blue smoke drifting slowly through the air. But before dissipating completely, his voice exploded like thunder in Chen Ji's ears:

"Young master, the fate of Chapter Seven Hundred is not an ending, but a beginning!"

That voice carried some indescribable power, as if crossing the boundaries of time and space, directly branding itself into the depths of Chen Ji's soul.

Chen Ji stood by the window, gazing at the rising morning sun in the east, speechless for a long time.

The fate of Chapter Seven Hundred.

That was the ending of the entire Tianji Record, the moment when the Eye of Heavenly Mandate's power reached its peak. At that moment, the recording of destiny would be completed, and the Eye of Heavenly Mandate would gain unprecedented power.

But what if—

What if someone could, before the fate of Chapter Seven Hundred was completed, break free from outside of destiny?

A smile slowly curved Chen Ji's lips, that smile carrying a hint of madness, yet also a hint of determination.

"Interesting..." he murmured to himself, "It seems I need to re-examine this 'chess game'."
